newsitem.title: MOROCCO: MOROCCAN BOURSE ENDS SESSION 0.30 PCT HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: MOROCCAN BOURSE ENDS SESSION 0.30 PCT HIGHER.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange rose 0.30 percent after its two-hour trading on Monday, pursuing its buoyant trend due to increasing demand for liquid stocks, a broker said.
The all-share index closed at 480.93 points form 479.48 points on Friday.
"The bourse has gained momentum since the beginning of the year due to investors' increasing confidence...But share prices remains too high," an analyst at Upline Securities stockbroker said.
Upline Securities index, which tracks the ten most liquid stocks rose 0.08 percent to close at 64,231 points compared with Friday's session.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private group which has a market capitalisation of more than 10.6 billion dirhams, rose four dirhams to close at 620 dirhams.
The day's strongest performer was consumer credit firm CREDOR which was floated on the bourse in December. It jumped 18 dirhans to close at 617 dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market second largest capitalisation, was traded at 712 dirhams unchanged compared with the previous session.
Wafabank, a liquid stock, rose seven dirhams to close at 607 dirhams. The bank purchased 100 percent stock of Spanish Uniban bank worth $28 million in December.
Morocco's second largest private conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement, lost five dirhams to close at 560 dirhams.
The traded volume on the official market was 62.8 million dirhams against 60.4 million on Friday.
